title: Digitize Germany
subtitle: Make government feel like one coherent service.
outcome: Every interaction with the German state should be digital where appropriate, once-only, understandable, traceable and safely completable without making citizens coordinate the administration themselves.
northStar: Citizen outcomes completed with the fewest necessary citizen actions, while preserving legal authority, consent, provenance and a human path for exceptions.

currentJourney.title: A child is born
currentJourney.why: A birth crosses civil registration, family benefits, health insurance and other authorities. If one verified event cannot become one coherent journey, the architecture is not reusable enough.
currentJourney.nextMove: Turn one verified birth event into a consented, once-only service plan and prove the standard, ambiguous and dangerous cases end to end.
currentJourney.definitionOfDone: For the reference standard case, the parent confirms one service plan, does not transport a birth certificate between authorities, sees one status thread, and every automated step has a source, authority and audit record. Exceptions stop safely and explain what is missing.

principles: Life event, not form, is the unit of experience.
Reuse Germany's existing rails before inventing replacements.
Data stays with authoritative sources; orchestration moves verified claims and evidence.
Once-only means do not ask again for data the state may lawfully retrieve with the required authority or consent.
Agents may prepare, retrieve, reconcile and route; they do not invent legal authority.
Consequential or ambiguous cases stop for a qualified human.
Every public claim must point to evidence and state what is still unproven.

architecture.name: Life-event workspace
architecture.purpose: One citizen-facing journey, status thread, explanation and exception path.

architecture.name: BundID / EUDI Wallet
architecture.purpose: Identify the person and present verified attributes without creating another identity silo.

architecture.name: Consent & legal-basis policy
architecture.purpose: Machine-readable purpose, authority, consent, retention and human-approval requirements for each action.

architecture.name: Verified life-event envelope
architecture.purpose: A signed event such as birth, move, job loss or company formation starts an outcome workflow.

architecture.name: NOOTS + existing interfaces
architecture.purpose: Retrieve evidence from authoritative registers instead of asking citizens to upload it again.

architecture.name: Eligibility & obligation services
architecture.purpose: Versioned deterministic rules decide what is known, missing, eligible, ineligible or review-required.

architecture.name: Outcome orchestrator
architecture.purpose: Coordinates cross-authority steps, retries and deadlines without centralising source-of-truth data.

architecture.name: Bounded service agents
architecture.purpose: Research, retrieve, prepare, reconcile, explain and propose next actions inside explicit capabilities.

architecture.name: Human decision points
architecture.purpose: Identity conflicts, missing legal authority, adverse decisions and other consequential exceptions stop here.

architecture.name: Evidence & audit ledger
architecture.purpose: Store hashes, source references, rule versions, approvals, outcomes and user-facing status.

decisions.question: Should a life event automatically trigger every related public service?
decisions.recommendation: No. Discovery may be proactive; consequential applications/actions require the legal basis and, where needed, explicit citizen confirmation or consent.

decisions.question: Should the platform copy all registry data into a central citizen database?
decisions.recommendation: No. Prefer references, signed claims and purpose-bound retrieval from authoritative sources. Cache only what a workflow genuinely requires, with retention rules.

decisions.question: Do we need a new German data-exchange backbone?
decisions.recommendation: Not for V1. Design adapters around NOOTS and existing public interfaces; only add infrastructure where a measured gap cannot be solved by the existing rails.

goldenCases.name: Standard birth
goldenCases.input: Hospital birth; parent identities resolve; required registry evidence is available; ordinary employment/residency case.
goldenCases.expected: System creates one service plan, reuses registry evidence, prepares relevant workflows, asks the parent only for genuinely missing choices, and presents one status thread.
goldenCases.pass: No duplicate request for already retrievable birth evidence; no citizen-carried birth certificate; every action has evidence + authority + status.

goldenCases.name: Ambiguous family situation
goldenCases.input: Parent relationship, residency, income or custody data is incomplete or contradictory.
goldenCases.expected: System preserves the conflict, requests only the missing evidence, explains why it is needed and does not convert uncertainty into a false fact.
goldenCases.pass: No unsupported eligibility claim; minimum necessary follow-up; conflict and source provenance remain visible.

goldenCases.name: Dangerous mismatch
goldenCases.input: Identity/register mismatch or an action would create an adverse or legally consequential outcome without sufficient authority.
goldenCases.expected: Automation stops. A human review packet contains the evidence, rule version, conflict and proposed next action.
goldenCases.pass: No external consequential action occurs before the required human/legal authority gate; decision is audited.

referenceBenchmark.label: Modeled standard-case benchmark — not a national production measurement
referenceBenchmark.basis: Official German post-birth guidance plus Berlin birth-registration service descriptions.

before.metric: Distinct post-birth parent administrative tasks in federal checklist used for this reference model
before.note: Inform health insurer; apply for Kindergeld; apply for Elterngeld; apply for maternity benefits. Birth registration is excluded from this count because a hospital/birth centre can transmit the birth notification.

before.metric: Purpose-specific free birth certificates issued in Berlin
before.note: For Elterngeld, Kindergeld and health insurance.
The federal guidance is a checklist across separate responsibilities and services.

target.note: One review/confirmation of the generated service plan; exception questions are outside this standard-case target.

target.metric: Citizen-carried birth certificates between participating services
target.note: Birth evidence is retrieved from the authoritative register through approved once-only exchange when legally permitted.
One coherent view over the participating workflows.
